Right: Tom eats rice at home. Wrong: Eats rice Tom at home.

events.quote: The rule: add -ed to many verbs to show the action is finished.
Right: On Tuesday he fixed the bike. Wrong: On Tuesday he fix the bike.
With regular verbs we add -ed for finished actions in the past
The rule: after can, use the plain verb with no -s, even with he or she.
Right: She can sing. Wrong: She can sings.
Rule: for a plan, use am, is or are, then going to, then the action.
Right: We are going to swim on Sunday. Wrong: We going to swim on Sunday.

events.quote: The rule: after can, use the plain verb with no -s.
Right: He can sing. Wrong: He can sings.
In English, a simple sentence goes: subject + verb + object, and place or time goes at the end.
So the rule is: start each sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop.
Right: Our cat is black. Wrong: our cat is black

Rule: use "at" before a clock time, like 9:00 or 6:30.
Right: "We eat lunch at 12:30." Wrong: "We eat lunch in 12:30."
